Package com.datastax.oss.driver.api.querybuilder.select

Interface Select

  • All Superinterfaces:
    BuildableQuery, OngoingSelection, OngoingWhereClause<Select>
    public interface Select
extends OngoingSelection, OngoingWhereClause<Select>, BuildableQuery
    A complete SELECT query.

    It knows about the table and at least one selector, and is therefore buildable. Additional selectors and clauses can still be added before building.

      • groupBy

        @NonNull
Select groupBy​(@NonNull
               Iterable<Selector> selectors)
        Adds the provided GROUP BY clauses to the query.

        As of version 4.0, Apache Cassandra only allows grouping by columns, therefore you can use the shortcuts groupByColumns(Iterable) or groupByColumnIds(Iterable).

      • orderByIds

        @NonNull
Select orderByIds​(@NonNull
                  Map<com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.CqlIdentifier,​com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.metadata.schema.ClusteringOrder> orderings)
        Adds the provided ORDER BY clauses to the query.

        They will be appended in the iteration order of the provided map. If an ordering was already defined for a given identifier, it will be removed and the new ordering will appear in its position in the provided map.

      • orderBy

        @NonNull
default Select orderBy​(@NonNull
                       Map<String,​com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.metadata.schema.ClusteringOrder> orderings)
        Shortcut for orderByIds(Map) with the columns specified as case-insensitive names. They will be wrapped with CqlIdentifier.fromCql(String).

        Note that it's possible for two different case-insensitive names to resolve to the same identifier, for example "foo" and "Foo"; if this happens, a runtime exception will be thrown.

        Throws:
        IllegalArgumentException - if two names resolve to the same identifier.

      • orderBy

        @NonNull
Select orderBy​(@NonNull
               com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.CqlIdentifier columnId,
               @NonNull
               com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.metadata.schema.ClusteringOrder order)
        Adds the provided ORDER BY clause to the query.

        If an ordering was already defined for this identifier, it will be removed and the new clause will be appended at the end of the current list for this query.

      • limit

        @NonNull
Select limit​(int limit)
        Adds a LIMIT clause to this query with a literal value.

        If this method or limit(BindMarker) is called multiple times, the last value is used.

      • limit

        @NonNull
Select limit​(@Nullable
             BindMarker bindMarker)
        Adds a LIMIT clause to this query with a bind marker.

        To create the argument, use one of the factory methods in QueryBuilder, for example bindMarker().

        If this method or limit(int) is called multiple times, the last value is used. null can be passed to cancel a previous limit.

      • perPartitionLimit

        @NonNull
Select perPartitionLimit​(int limit)
        Adds a PER PARTITION LIMIT clause to this query with a literal value.

        If this method or perPartitionLimit(BindMarker) is called multiple times, the last value is used.

      • perPartitionLimit

        @NonNull
Select perPartitionLimit​(@Nullable
                         BindMarker bindMarker)
        Adds a PER PARTITION LIMIT clause to this query with a bind marker.

        To create the argument, use one of the factory methods in QueryBuilder, for example bindMarker().

        If this method or perPartitionLimit(int) is called multiple times, the last value is used. null can be passed to cancel a previous limit.

      • allowFiltering

        @NonNull
Select allowFiltering()
        Adds an ALLOW FILTERING clause to this query.

        This method is idempotent, calling it multiple times will only add a single clause.

      • usingTimeout

        @NonNull
Select usingTimeout​(@NonNull
                    com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.data.CqlDuration timeout)
        Adds a USING TIMEOUT clause to this statement with a literal value. Setting a value of null will remove the USING TIMEOUT clause on this statement.

        If this method or usingTimeout(BindMarker) is called multiple times, the value from the last invocation is used.

        Parameters:
        timeout - A timeout value controlling server-side query timeout.

      • usingTimeout

        @NonNull
Select usingTimeout​(@NonNull
                    BindMarker timeout)
        Adds a USING TIMEOUT clause to this statement with a bind marker. Setting a value of null will remove the USING TIMEOUT clause on this statement.

        If this method or usingTimeout(CqlDuration) is called multiple times, the value from the last invocation is used.

        Parameters:
        timeout - A bind marker understood as CqlDuration controlling server-side query timeout.

      • bypassCache

        @NonNull
Select bypassCache()
        Adds an BYPASS CACHE clause to this query.

        This method is idempotent, calling it multiple times will only add a single clause.
